newsitem.title: INDIA: India's FICCI sees time lag in industrial recovery.
newsitem.headline: India's FICCI sees time lag in industrial recovery.

text.p: The Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI) said on Friday that a survey of business firms showed that a current slowdown in industrial growth could take a year to bottom out.

"The slowdown in industrial growth will bottom out only by the end of the current financial year, and in the first quarter of the financial year 1998/98, industry will grow between 10.5 and 11.5 percent," it said in a statement.
Industrial production grew by 7.5 percent in the first 10 months of 1997/98 (April-March) compared with 11.7 percent in the same period of 1996/97, the government said on Wednesday.

FICCI said a survey of 175 firms in the large, medium and small industry sectors showed that the current slowdown, although temporary, could take time to ease. But there were positive factors aiding recovery, it said.

"This trend will be reversed due to the combined effect of the budget of 1997/98, the new credit policy, relaxation in external commercial borrowings (ECBs) and a host of other steps which are being taken by the government," it said.

The lower house of parliament on Friday passed the Finance Bill giving shape to import duty and personal taxation cuts that Finance Minister P. Chidambaram proposed in his budget for 1997/98, presented on February 28.
Borrowing rates have fallen since the Reserve Bank of India eased the interest rate regime in a six-month credit policy announced last month.

"Eighty percent of the respondents to the FICCI survey based their rationale for bottoming out of the slowing down to the fact that there is a 'lag effect' for the policy framework to show its results," the FICCI statement said.
